# Trail Wars — approved peach/plum UI fidelity pass (UI ONLY)

## Objective
Rebuild the user's **approved** TRAIL WARS reference screenshot into a real, responsive Roblox UI with high visual fidelity. This is an **appearance/UI-only sprint**, not a gameplay port. Do not extract, copy, or implement Curve Fever Pro's proprietary game code. Do not rewrite server systems or enable real purchases.

## Authoritative input
The user approved a 1672×941 PNG showing the **"MAKE IT YOURS" customization page**:
- warm peach/apricot background and soft orange accent shapes
- chunky cream/orange TRAIL WARS logo with dark plum outline and turquoise ring
- left navigation with glossy plum rounded buttons; active SHOP button orange in the reference
- central item cards (Ring Core, Dashed Trail), coin cost pills, STARTER CORE/TRAIL owned states
- cream-framed dark-plum top-down trail preview, turquoise YOU ring, orange/coral trails
- top coin + profile, top Home/back, large orange VIEW ITEM CTA
- rounded 3D/clay-like bevels, subtle highlights, shadows, bold bubble lettering
- clear cosmetic-only/purchases-unavailable labels

**Required:** Place the exact user-approved PNG at `design/reference/approved_customize_1672x941.png` before work starts. If it is not present locally, ask for that file; do not substitute a newly generated screenshot or earlier charcoal/yellow mockup. Do not assume other previously generated concept sheets are approved.

## Recommended tools (evaluate, don't blindly replace architecture)
1. **Figma** (or equivalent layered design editor) for tracing the screenshot and authoring reusable source assets; maintain editable layer design and export PNGs/assets with transparent edges.
2. **Roblox ImageLabel/ImageButton nine-slice** for rich glossy beveled scalable buttons, cards, cream frame, selected borders, cost pills. Export separate skins (normal, pressed/selected, disabled where needed), not giant flattened screen art. Use native UIStroke, UICorner, UIGradient and plain frames only where they actually match the artwork.
3. **Existing componentized native Luau + Rojo** as source of truth for functional GUI instances and event wiring.
4. **UI Labs 14 preexisting stories** for isolated visual checks. A Figma→Roblox converter (e.g. FigBloxUI or open-source figrbx) may accelerate basic editable layout import; test a sample component first and measure fidelity, asset ownership, licensing, time, and maintenance cost. Do not put a fragile converter in the critical path without proof.
5. **Image assets as designed**, imported into the project/experience through approved Studio asset workflows. Avoid relying on unpublished placeholders or fake Roblox asset IDs.

## Phased execution
**A. Preserve project.** Start from latest main (last verified commit d7b7480), create a feature branch, confirm the 40-test baseline and existing working UI/business systems. Do not delete anything.

**B. Design reconstruction, BEFORE mass coding.** Overlay/tracing reference at 1672×941. Extract a style token sheet: colors sampled from reference, type hierarchy, padding, corner geometry, highlights, drop shadows, bevel depths, stroke thickness, button hitboxes, icon sizes, original asset specs. Recreate the screenshot in layered form. Define a small reusable skin kit with 9-slice coordinates and PNG dimensions. Save both editable source and exports; version assets sensibly.

**C. Single-screen proof.** Implement the approved `Customize` screen visually first at a matching 1672×941 test viewport with representative mock data. Preserve all existing click and ownership behaviors. Use native TextLabels for text, prices, counts and accessibility; use reusable 9-slice assets for visual shells; render the trail preview independently. Compare a real Roblox screenshot with the approved PNG using side-by-side and overlay/difference; document mismatches and fix them. Do NOT claim 'one-to-one' merely because sizes roughly match. Ask user to approve the screenshot proof before propagating the style across the other routes.

**D. Rest of UI.** Design Home, Play/Queue, Shop, Profile, Settings, HUD, elimination and results with the same exact visual grammar. Mockup/preview screen-specific changes for approval if they aren't unambiguously defined by the reference. Do not introduce Ranked, Battle Pass, gems, time-limited offers, fake wins, or new currencies from unapproved generative art. Then implement approved appearances; leave mock gameplay states honestly labeled.

**E. Real responsiveness.** The 1672×941 reference is a desktop target, not a layout that should be uniformly shrunk. Use safe-area insets, responsive rearrangement and min hit areas, mobile scroll. Validate small phone portrait and landscape, tablet, desktop, gamepad focus, long numbers, larger fonts, and text wrapping.

**F. Performance & quality.** Avoid giant full-screen high-res sprites and gratuitous CanvasGroups; re-use skins/sprite atlases, optimize UI depth, minimize texture memory, animate only short intentional states, lazy-mount noncurrent screens and release connections. Keep server-authoritative ownership, no live commerce. No 3D lobby or avatar imagery.

## Explicit acceptance evidence
- Reference screenshot file present in design reference folder.
- Layered source / reusable assets and nine-slice inventory with usage docs.
- Screenshot of actual Roblox `Customize` screen at reference resolution + side-by-side overlay and list of fixed differences.
- Screenshots of phone and desktop variants, no clipping.
- Retained navigation and sample equip flows.
- Existing 40 foundation assertions and builds still pass; any UI additions tested.
- No gameplay code introduced; gameplay remains mock.
- No production purchases, fake product IDs, reference game code, or copied proprietary assets.
- GitHub feature branch/PR with QA evidence; do not merge or publish before user visual approval.

## Tool budget
Source-first as in issue #1: prioritize Figma/export/local image scripts/CLI/Rojo/UI Labs. Use Studio only for batched visual verification. Do not relaunch Steam or REA unless specifically needed for an unresolved approved-UI question; here it should not be needed.

# Updated direction from owner — FULL UI SYSTEM FIRST, responsive and playful (2026-11-09)

**This comment supersedes issue #2's old order of operations where Codex immediately reconstructs the one approved Customize screen.** The exact approved peach/plum MAKE IT YOURS screenshot stays the **visual anchor**, but first plan the **whole UI/UX system** before extensive implementation. Do not discard existing work.

## Where we are
- Main: `d7b7480`, working source-first Luau/Rojo UI foundation with mocks, server systems, 14 UI Labs stories, and verified baseline tests.
- Active branch: `feature/approved-customize-fidelity` at `6c16f5a`. Contains exact approved PNG `design/reference/approved_customize_1672x941.png`, design research, and `design/approved-customize/toolchain.md`.
- Chosen proposed asset workflow so far: editable layered SVG/JSON, generated reusable PNGs, native text/buttons, 9-slice, Luau/Rojo. **This is a hypothesis, not a mandate.** Reassess pragmatically if real fidelity or scaling tests prove it wrong. Never use a flattened screenshot as the final UI.

## Owner's intent
The UI must evoke the **playful, accessible, tactile, delightful polish associated with great Nintendo games** (high confidence, consistent visual language, responsive bounce, charming sound confirmation, obvious navigation and reward moments). Do not copy Nintendo characters, icons, trademarks or specific screens. Avoid visual noise, over-decoration, grindy simulator tropes, and inert buttons.

It must adapt correctly to **every supported viewport and input method**, not just a 1672×941 desktop mockup. “Looks accurate” on one resolution is insufficient. Achieve fidelity at the desktop reference and deliberately reorganize content on compact devices instead of applying one blanket UIScale.

## Mandatory phase 1: comprehensive information architecture and complete inventory BEFORE more UI coding
1. Audit every existing route/component, state and contract in the repository and collect a route-state inventory. Preserve functional systems and distinguish existing, proposed, deferred and mock-only features.
2. Define every screen needed across the user's actual game:
   - boot/profile loading, offline/failed load and retry;
   - first-launch controls tutorial and input changes;
   - Home/Play, mode selector *only if justified*, matchmaking queue/cancel/error;
   - prematch/ready/countdown, gameplay HUD, pause/leave confirmation, elimination/spectate, victory/defeat/results/rematch;
   - Customize: owned/locked/equipped, core/trail selection, preview, item details and unlock path;
   - Shop: catalog, selection, owned/off-sale, affordability, purchase confirmation/cancel/pending/success/failure/reconciliation and commerce-unavailable;
   - Profile/stats, progression/reward explanation (do not invent win/XP data), Settings (controls, audio, display/accessibility), help/feedback;
   - cross-cutting dialogs, tooltips, notifications, connectivity/rejoin, empty/loading/error states.
   - Social, ranked, battle pass, extra currencies, timed offers, leaderboards etc are **future options**, not automatically launch requirements. Explicitly decide MVP/later/excluded and avoid fake active features.
3. Produce a navigation flow graph, screen-by-screen inventory, complete state matrix, back/focus rules, input mapping, CTA hierarchy, and how each screen transitions.
4. Record concise user flows (new player to first match, first equip, locked item to earn/unlock, purchase cancellation/error, elimination to rematch, reconnect/recovery). Target low friction and short time to Play; test rather than assert.
5. Define design tokens and component system: `ScreenShell`, `SafeArea`, `TopBar`, `ResponsiveNav`, `PrimaryButton`, `SecondaryButton`, `Pill`, `Tab`, `Card`, `Modal`, `Toast`, `ItemTile`, `CurrencyDisplay`, `Progress`, `TrailPreview`, `SettingsRow`, `HUD`, `Feedback`. Define normal/hover/focus/pressed/disabled/selected/loading/error variants, disposal and state contracts.
6. Document a meaningful, cohesive Nintendo-**feeling** interaction philosophy: anticipatory press/physical depth, crisp but restrained bounce on release, short non-annoying audio cues, focus visibility, delightful win/reward acknowledgment, no excessive constant animation, reduced-motion fallback and mute. Explain timings and sound budgets as hypotheses for testing.

Deliver `design/ui-master-plan/` docs: `screen-inventory.md`, `navigation-and-state-machine.md`, `components-and-tokens.md`, `adaptive-layout-contract.md`, `interaction-and-motion.md`, `implementation-plan.md`, `qa-matrix.md`.

## Mandatory phase 2: REAL responsive strategy
- Compute layout from **available safe-area content rectangle and parent width/height**, not only platform/device name or raw screen pixel dimensions. Support orientation, aspect ratio, safe-area insets, notch/console overscan, viewport resize and changing preferred input.
- Use platform-native `UIListLayout`/flex/grid as appropriate, `AutomaticSize`, `AutomaticCanvasSize`, `UISizeConstraint`, `UITextSizeConstraint`, `UIAspectRatioConstraint` *selectively*, `AnchorPoint`, 9-slice for decorative shells; use `UIScale` only when it aids readability or local component scale—not as the sole responsiveness technique. Beware conflicting constraints and automatic sizing loops.
- Define adaptive **composition modes** by container measurements (not hard-coded assumptions): spacious landscape, compact landscape, portrait/tablet and narrow portrait. Explain which panels stack, wrap, scroll, become collapsible, or stay fixed. Keep the Play CTA and critical Back/Close/Cancel accessible without offscreen hiding.
- Touch targets: design for at least ~48 logical pixels where practical; verify actual effective hit rectangles. Avoid tiny text or tap targets caused by downscaling.
- Landscape gameplay HUD must preserve unobstructed sightlines/trail visibility; phone touch steering zones should be independent of menu UI.
- Test at representative sizes incl. 320×568, 360×640, 390×844, 768×1024, 1280×720, 1672×941 and ultrawide, both portrait and landscape where relevant, with 100%, 125%, 150% text. Test long names, large values, long localized labels, no overlap/clipping, no unreadable text, no inaccessible scroll, no status-bar collisions. These are starting viewports, not a finite claim of supporting literally every size.
- Use real Studio engine tests and manually verify touch/controller semantics. A Frame-size simulation does not prove safe-area behavior or hardware performance.

## Mandatory phase 3: visual proposals BEFORE broad implementation
- Build a complete design board / representative mockups for ALL relevant routes and core state variants in the approved peach/plum/orange/turquoise tactile style. **Do not reinterpret the approved screenshot as permission to change gameplay or add arbitrary systems.**
- At minimum present Home, Play/Queue, Customize, Item Details, Shop, Purchase, Profile, Settings, HUD, Spectator, Results, core error/loading states; include both spacious and compact layouts.
- Keep real Roblox dynamic text, counters and controls editable. Establish a reusable asset/slices inventory and precisely document widths/corners/highlights/shadows. Determine source files and original art ownership.
- **Stop for owner approval of the complete system and representative screens**, not just one page. Existing approved Customize screenshot is approved as a *style reference*; new screen compositions are not automatically approved.

## Mandatory phase 4: after approval, implement in reusable Luau source
- Preserve existing business/economy modules and mocks; code first via existing Rojo structure, with UI Labs stories and fixture variants for every shared component and each major screen state.
- Prefer data-driven rendering and route state machines, scoped connections/tweens, accessibility and input abstractions, sane mount/unmount, no per-frame rebuilding.
- Make it beautiful **and** efficient: 9-slice selective skins, few reusable atlases, native text, cached assets, low image overdraw/transparency, short animations, appropriate texture-resolution tiers. Measure actual CPU frame costs and memory; never invent benchmark performance.
- Keep purchased items, balance, failed purchases and mocked match results clearly truthful. No live monetization or gameplay implementation in this task.
- Batch actual Studio review checkpoints. Compare screen captures against the approved reference at desktop, and separately assess intentional compact reflow. Maintain automated layout, navigation, and engine checks. Do not claim 1:1 on every viewport: distinguish exact reference fidelity from responsive equivalence.
- Push work to a feature branch/PR. Do not merge, publish, or activate monetization without approval.

## CRITICAL engineering rule: abandon dead ends
Codex has explicit permission and responsibility to **change tools, libraries, asset construction and implementation strategy when evidence indicates a dead end**.
- Timebox experimental approaches; after ~2 meaningful failed attempts or failure to reach measured visual/performance goals, stop repeating the same technique.
- Write a short technical decision record: what was attempted, evidence of failure, alternative options, expected tradeoffs and recommended pivot.
- Try a small proof-of-concept of the alternative before migrating the entire UI. Prefer reversible changes and feature branches.
- Do not cling to Figma, SVG, image slicing, a particular converter, a font, a framework, or the prior code merely because already invested. Preserve working code and assets before pivoting. Avoid endless tool experimentation and pointless GUI loops.
- Do not silently abandon major approved style goals; distinguish implementation pivots from visual-design deviations, and seek owner review when the latter are necessary.

## Immediate next output
1. Show exactly what is present on current branch and which previous audit work is reusable.
2. Deliver the complete UI screen/state plan, responsive layout contract and modular component architecture in source-controlled docs.
3. Produce a staged visual plan/mockups of the full system.
4. **Pause for the owner's approval before the broad UI rebuild.**

Sources to check for current engine APIs:
- https://create.roblox.com/docs/production/publishing/adaptive-design
- https://create.roblox.com/docs/projects/cross-platform
- https://create.roblox.com/docs/ui/size-modifiers
- https://create.roblox.com/docs/production/game-design/ui-ux-design

Keep this issue's previous visual-fidelity acceptance conditions, but follow this new order of execution.
